what: THE ONE PERMITTED REBUILD (runner-compatibility defect class, diagnosed in pins-planning-baseline-001): stage 0 runs the worker-side minimal probe probe_category_predict.py (synthetic frames, the same dependency ranges the baseline job installs) to settle whether the verbatim train.py predict path accepts category dtypes under the installed xgboost - baseline-001 measured xgboost 3.4.1 inplace_predict rejecting all nine category-dtype columns AND the object-dtype floor_space_sqm at model.predict_proba even though enable_categorical=True was set at fit. Writer changes only, both fixes in the same rebuild: (1) num() maps unparseable publisher prose ('Under 200 sq m floorspace', 6 eval rows) to '' missing, so no numeric column can arrive object-dtype; (2) if the probe verdict is rejected, the nine string-categorical columns (lpa_name, ons_lpa_code, casework_type, procedure, development_type, appeal_type_reason, appeal_reason, type_detail, link_status) ship as integer codes 1..N over the pooled eligible panel's sorted distinct non-blank values, blank stays missing - codes documented in quality.json categorical_coding/measurements/feature_evidence, full value->code table in the collected summary.json. Everything else is byte-for-byte unchanged from pins-planning-001: same pinned GOV.UK Excel bytes, same frame and dedup, same splits on the validation instant (train < 2020 valid, eval 2020-2021, holdout >= 2022), same per-decision-year fixture, same LPA-history construction - so split counts must equal 001 exactly (train 54,834/17,048; eval 28,104/8,469; holdout 56,326/17,705) and references must reproduce 001's figures (procedure_type 0.5551, lpa_hist 0.5414, persistence 0.5045, degenerate calendar control). Full worker order: probe -> construct -> qualify (gate 1.5.0, full artifact) -> exact-byte accept -> simple references (score.py, post-acceptance, eval rows only, holdout never opened). Stopping condition: a second failure of this defect class after this rebuild means stop and re-target - no pins-planning-003.
